rationale: Systematic clinical review of the literature demonstrates that sparse hair (hypotrichosis/alopecia) is present in 26 of 28 reported individuals (92.9%) with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome (GTPBP2 deficiency). This frequency surpasses all other non-neurological clinical manifestations, including skeletal abnormalities (23/28) and visual/ophthalmic impairment (18/28). Furthermore, longitudinal phenotypic characterization confirms that ectodermal manifestations such as sparse hair are age-dependent and become clinically prominent after early infancy, establishing sparse hair as the most sensitive non-neurological hallmark in post-infantile patients.

evidence.text: In a literature review of 28 individuals with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome, sparse hair was identified in 26 of 28 individuals (92.9%), which was more frequent than skeletal anomalies (23/28) or visual impairment (18/28), and tied with motor developmental delay (26/28).

source.title: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome: Exploring a novel GTPBP2 mutation and a literature review
source.quote: A large numbers of patients manifest motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), and speech disorder (24/28). Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28).

evidence.text: Clinical delineation shows that ectodermal findings (sparse hair, dental anomalies) in GTPBP2-associated neuro-ectodermal syndrome are age-dependent, becoming most prominent in older children and adolescents rather than at birth or during early infancy.

source.title: Clinical delineation of GTPBP2-associated neuro-ectodermal syndrome: Report of two new families and review of the literature
source.quote: Our findings suggest that some aspects of the clinical presentation appear to be age-related; brain iron accumulation may appear only after childhood, and the ectodermal findings and peripheral neuropathy are most prominent in older individuals.

evidence.text: Case report of Jaberi-Elahi syndrome caused by maternal UPD 6 highlights sparse hair as a recognized ectodermal hallmark of the disorder.

new_directions.question_text: What is the precise onset timeline of hypotrichosis in infants carrying biallelic GTPBP2 loss-of-function variants between 6 and 24 months of life?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the exact developmental window in which hair thinning or loss manifests will establish diagnostic utility during early pediatric screening before classic neurodegenerative signs emerge.

new_directions.question_text: How does hair shaft microscopy and trichoscopy in Jaberi-Elahi syndrome differ from other neuro-ectodermal and mitochondrial disorders with alopecia?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing hair shaft structural phenotypes could offer a rapid, non-invasive bedside tool to distinguish GTPBP2 deficiency from overlapping complex neurodegenerative conditions.
